title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Purpose

This page consolidates Redwood's employee-facing policies and guides for working at Redwood: role definitions and career ladders, performance and promotion processes, benefits and perks, an end-to-end hiring and onboarding overview, and a short internal tools guide for day-to-day operations. It is maintained by People Ops with technical review from Engineering and Product.

Contents
1) Intro and philosophy
2) Roles & career ladders
3) Performance, promotion, and leveling process
4) Hiring and onboarding overview (hiring workflow, interview rubrics, first-week checklist)
5) Benefits & perks summary
6) Internal tools quick reference
7) Ownership and contacts
8) FAQ and links

1) Intro and philosophy
- Redwood's people philosophy centers on clarity, growth, and operational excellence.
- We provide transparent role expectations, a repeatable promotion process, comprehensive benefits, and tooling to enable engineers and cross-functional partners to ship and operate production inference features.
- This page is intended for new hires, managers, and hiring committees as the single source of truth for day-to-day people processes.

2) Roles & career ladders
- High-level role families (examples):
  - Engineering: Software Engineer I/II/Senior/Staff/Principal; SRE/Infrastructure/Platform specializations.
  - Applied ML: Applied ML Engineer / ML Engineer II / Senior ML Engineer / Staff ML Engineer.
  - Product: PM Associate / PM / Senior PM / Group PM.
  - Design: Product Designer I/II/Senior.
  - GTM: Account Executive / Customer Success Manager / Sales Engineer / Manager levels.
- Each ladder contains three canonical sections: Impact, Scope, and Skills. Managers use these to write role-specific job descriptions.

Sample career ladder excerpt (Engineering):
| Level | Impact | Scope | Expected outcomes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| SE I | Contributes to a single feature area with mentorship | 1-2 small services or components | Delivers well-scoped tasks with tests and docs |
| SE II | Owns modules, capable of independent design | Multiple components, cross-team work | Designs moderately complex features, mentors juniors |
| Senior | Leads feature initiatives, influences architecture | Cross-product features and performance goals | Delivers high-impact projects, drives postmortems and improvements |
| Staff | Technical lead across teams; drives system-level improvements | Company-level infrastructure and performance | Shapes platform roadmap; mentors senior engineers |

How to use ladders:
- Managers: map incoming hires to a level during offer stage and record the rationale in the hiring packet.
- ICs and managers: use ladders as a baseline for performance reviews and promotion packets.
- Compensation team: uses ladder level when calibrating leveling and comp offers.

3) Performance, promotion, and leveling process
- Review cadence: formal performance reviews are quarterly with a calibration cycle each review.
- Promotion cycle: rolling eligibility with check-ins during quarterly reviews; recommended promotion packet timeline: 8-12 weeks of documented impact plus manager endorsement.
- Promotion packet required artifacts:
  1. Summary: 300-500 words explaining the candidate's impact and readiness.
  2. Evidence: list of projects, metrics (latency/cost savings, availability improvements), code links, design docs, and peer feedback.
  3. Manager recommendation: explicit level and rationale.
- Rubric highlights: Scope, Technical impact, Ownership, Mentorship, Cross-team influence, Outcome-driven delivery.
- Appeals: If denied, a 1:1 with People Ops and the manager to review feedback and create a 90-day development plan.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview
- Hiring philosophy: hire for curiosity, ownership, and ability to ship at scale. We emphasize production experience (ops, performance tradeoffs) for platform and infra roles.
- Standard hiring workflow (numbered steps):
  1) Requisition created and posted internally; hiring manager drafts role brief and scorecard.
  2) Sourcing & screening: Recruiter screens, schedules initial hiring manager phone screen.
  3) Interview loop: Technical screen (coding/system design) + Take-home/Exercise (if applicable) + Cross-functional interviews (product, infra, security). Use standardized rubrics.
  4) Calibration and debrief: Interviewers submit scores and narrative; hiring committee conducts calibration.
  5) Offer: People Ops generates offer, manager approves, recruiter closes.
  6) Onboarding kickoff: Pre-start checklist and first-week plan are shared.

Interview rubrics (examples):
- Coding: Problem solving, testability, tradeoff discussion, code clarity.
- System design: Requirement elicitation, scalability, cost/latency tradeoffs, operational considerations (rollouts, metrics, caching).
- Culture fit: Ownership examples, collaboration, incident behaviour.

First-week onboarding checklist (for managers & new hires):
- Before day 1: Laptop provisioned, Okta + SSO enabled, Slack invite, Confluence access, security training assigned.
- Day 1: Welcome session with People Ops, team intro, 90-day goals discussion, initial 1:1 scheduled.
- Day 2-5: Quickstarts: local dev environment, runbook reading, pair programming session, onboarding ticket to ship a small doc or fix.
- First 30/60/90 milestones: 30d: merge first non-trivial PR, 60d: own a small feature, 90d: lead a retro or present a learning.

New manager checklist (first 90 days):
1) Create onboarding plan for direct reports.
2) Review open PRs and roadmap.
3) Schedule 1:1 cadence and team syncs.
4) Complete manager training (People Ops workshop).

5) Benefits & perks summary
- Core benefits (example summaries):
  - Health: Medical, dental, vision with multiple plan options and HSA.
  - Financial: 401(k) with company match, RSUs or equity grant at offer.
  - Time off: Flexible PTO policy, 10+ observed company holidays, parental leave (primary/secondary), and caregiver leave.
  - Family support: Fertility and adoption assistance program.
  - Professional development: $2,000/year learning stipend, conference allowance, internal training.
  - Wellness: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), mental health benefits, and periodic wellness stipends.
  - Remote/hybrid support: Home office stipend and quarterly co-working allowance.

Benefits enrollment timeline:
- New hires: benefits portal opens on day 1; coverage effective first of the next month unless otherwise specified.

Perks & culture programs:
- Quarterly offsites, monthly all-hands, AMA with execs, affinity groups, mentorship program, drop-in office hours with founders.

6) Internal tools quick reference
- Slack: primary synchronous communication. Join channels: #all, #eng, #team-{your-team}. Use huddle for quick syncs.
- Confluence: canonical docs and runbooks. Update the team wiki pages for anything you change in infra.
- Jira (or Linear): issue tracking and sprint boards. Create tickets for customer-impacting incidents and label severity.
- Okta / SSO: single-sign-on for access to AWS/GCP, GitHub, Jira, Confluence. Report MFA or access issues to security@redwood.com.
- GitHub: code reviews, trunk-based development with feature flags. Use PR templates and include testing plan and performance considerations.
- CI/CD: Build runs in our internal pipeline (see eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build runbook). Ensure unit and integration tests run in PR.
- Deployments & staging: follow runbooks in eng-platform/runbooks; require two approvers for production deploys for high-risk repos.

Example command snippets (local dev):
- Setup repo (example):
  git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/example-service.git
  ./scripts/bootstrap.sh

- Basic CI status check (internal tool):
  cictl status --repo example-service --branch feature/your-thing
